effective.basis: Per-card ruling chronology from two archived official documents: the UDE Card Rulings capture of 2005-06-16 expressly permits activation with no "Dark Magician" in hand, Deck or Graveyard subject to verification (the effect then disappearing); Konami's yugioh-card.com Card FAQ capture of 2008-12-15 expressly forbids activation in that case.

changes.historical_text: Each time you or your opponent activates 1 Spell Card, put 1 Spell Counter on this card (max. 3). Tribute this card with 3 Spell Counters on it to Special Summon 1 "Dark Magician" from your hand, Deck, or Graveyard.
changes.summary: Period procedure plus a per-card activation ruling, not a text erratum: the GOAT script reduces s.sptg to the free-zone test alone (the modern Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard over Deck, hand and Graveyard is removed), so the 3-Spell-Counter Tribute effect can be activated with no "Dark Magician" anywhere, and it proves the failure by revealing hand and Deck (Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_DECK+LOCATION_HAND); the Graveyard is already public); the modern script requires an available "Dark Magician" to activate and never reveals. Period rulings add that in the old era the effect simply disappeared on resolution.

review.notes: Chain starts at v1 (DR1-EN120, 2005-03-19), the text the GOAT variant carries exactly; v0 (MFC-065) predates it and states the same Main Phase Tribute in older phrasing. v1->v2->v3 (SDSC-EN007) ->v4 (DL15-EN001) ->v5 (LEDD-ENA06) are cosmetic: 'when that Spell resolves' merely prints the ruling already in force in 2005 ('You place a Spell Counter on this monster when the Spell Card resolves'), and both scripts place the counter in the resolution handler. Like Reinforcement of the Army and Rescue Cat, this card lost its fail-to-find allowance before the general verification procedure ended, so the shared 'search-verification' chronology is not used and the change is dated from the two archived captures instead: GOAT (2005-04-01) precedes 2005-06-16 and takes the historical implementation, Edison (2010-04-24) follows 2008-12-15 and takes the modern card. Residual not modelled as a version: after 2008-12-15 a whiff forced by a chain (e.g. the last "Dark Magician" removed in response) would presumably still have been verifiable until the general procedure ended; that intermediate state has no upstream implementation and no practical effect, so it is documented here rather than recorded as a gap. Remaining diff hunk (re:IsActiveType(TYPE_SPELL) vs re:IsSpellEffect()) is upstream idiom.
